details.publicNotes:
An aestival's ideal state of being is snoozing a hot summer day away in some comfortably inconvenient locale, ideally with a high vantage point. There are stories aplenty of aestivals falling asleep beneath a farmer's cart, tangled in the sails of a windmill, or upon a millstone ready to grind. To make matters worse, they are incredibly cranky when awoken and liable to wreak real havoc before grumpily stalking away to find a better napping spot.

During the rare times they are awake, aestivals enjoy watching laborers tend to the fields or children play in meadows and pastures (from a cushy, relaxed perch, of course). They have a particular love of work songs, children's rhymes, and lullabies, and it is said that breaking into one of these songs is one of the few ways an aestival can be calmed down from their incandescent anger.

Aestivals can go long stretches of time without eating. When they do choose to partake in food, they indulge in lavish feasts, often to the annoyance of those who originally owned the food. Yet aestivals are not entirely freeloaders in their communities. When monsters or other perils threaten the tranquility of their homes, they spring into action, placing themselves in harm's way to awaken their internal flames.

Seasonals are a cycle of four kinds of fey, each tied to one of the four seasons: vernals who embody spring's renewal and storming showers, aestivals who embody summer's lazy heat and burning passion, autumnals who embody the melancholy culling and reaping harvest of autumn, and hibernals who embody winter's quiet cheer.

Whatever the current season in the mortal world, seasonals wrap themselves in a metaphysical cloak of their own season's magic and carry the songs full of that season's surging emotions with them wherever they go in the mortal world or across the realm of Faerie. Whenever seasonals meet, shy hibernals typically prefer to amuse themselves by watching the antics of the other three kinds of fey, while vernals impatiently call for energetic contests, aestivals languidly nap until roused to fiery bursts of activity, and autumnals attempt to imbue a sense of stark responsibility in the rest of their compatriots. Exceptions exist, with those seasonals interacting with the others in ways unexpected based upon the stereotypes of their season.

Summer Solstice

If there's one time of year an aestival is certain to be active, it's during the summer solstice. On the longest day of the year, aestivals throw raucous celebrations filled with music and dancing, often encouraging those around them (through force, if necessary) to join in the festivities. On the summer solstice, the aestival is usually awakened, and until the sun sets they can choose whether or not to return to their languid state.

Suggested Monster Parts

Monster Parts 30/65/125 gp

Eligible Refinements weapons (bludgeoning), armor (light), skill items (Acrobatics, Athletics, Nature, Performance, Stealth)

Eligible Imbued Properties bane, burning barbs, charisma, constitution, energy resistant (fire, vitality), fire, fire shield, mind, mind shield, music, sensory (low-light vision), spells (Primal: environmental endurance, fireball, ignition), strength, time, wild

You snap your fingers and point at a target, which begins to smolder. Make a spell attack roll against the target's AC, dealing 2d4 fire damage on a hit. If the target is within your melee reach, you can choose to make a melee spell attack with the flame instead of a ranged spell attack, which increases all the spell's damage dice to d6s.

Critical Success The target takes double damage and 1d4 persistent fire damage.

Success The target takes full damage.

Heightened (+1) The initial damage increases by 1d4 and the persistent fire damage on a critical hit increases by 1d4.

@Damage[(@item.rank)d4[persistent,fire]]{Scaling Persistent Fire Damage}

@Damage[(@item.rank)d6[persistent,fire]]{Scaling Persistent Fire Damage (Melee)}

Your performance makes allies feel they can succeed at anything. This counts as having prepared to Aid your ally on a skill check of your choice. When you later use the Aid reaction, you can roll Performance instead of the normal skill check, and if you roll a failure, you get a success instead. If you are legendary in Performance, you automatically critically succeed.

The GM might rule that you can't use this ability if the act of encouraging your ally would interfere with the skill check (such as a check to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.VMozDqMMuK5kpoX4]{Sneak} quietly or maintain a disguise).

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-anachronism.spell-effects.Item.ITErgFRfydm1xmnW]{Spell Effect: Uplifting Overture}

Each creature in the area becomes drowsy and might fall asleep. A creature that falls @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} from this spell doesn't fall @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} or release what it's holding. This spell doesn't prevent creatures from waking up due to a successful Perception check, limiting its utility in combat.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes a -1 status penalty to Perception checks for 1 round.

Failure The creature falls Unconscious. If it's still Unconscious after 1 minute, it wakes up automatically.

Critical Failure The creature falls Unconscious. If it's still Unconscious after 1 hour, it wakes up automatically.

Heightened (4th) The creatures fall Unconscious for 1 round on a failure or 1 minute on a critical failure. They fall Prone and release what they're holding, and they can't attempt Perception checks to wake up. When the duration ends, the creature is sleeping normally instead of automatically waking up.

Aestivals are most often in their languid state, where they are permanently @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} and under the effects of @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.8xRzLhwGL7Dgy3EZ]. If they take damage from any source, they become awakened until the end of their next turn, losing the slowed condition and the effects of sanctuary. While awakened, they are @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} (the extra action can be used only to Stride, Climb, or Strike), and they deal an additional 4 fire damage with their Strikes and with their @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.6DfLZBl8wKIV03Iq] cantrip.

@UUID[Compendium.battlezoo-bestiary-es-pf2e.sf2e-effects.Item.F31w4PdoRtstZvZs]{Effect: Awakened}

Trigger A creature within the aestival's reach uses a move action or leaves a square during a move action it's using

Effect The aestival attempts an Athletics check to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.ge56Lu1xXVFYUnLP]{Trip} the creature. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the aestival's multiple attack penalty.

While the aestival is awakened, all terrain they move through becomes fiery, hazardous terrain, dealing @Damage[5[fire]] damage to any creature who moves into one of these squares. The hazardous terrain lasts until the start of the aestival's next turn.

An aestival's fists sap energy, much like a day of hard labor beneath a baking sun. An affected creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:21] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued}.

Requirements The aestival is awakened

Effect The aestival Strides or Climbs and then makes two fist Strikes against a single enemy. Apply the multiple attack penalty to these Strikes normally. If both Strikes succeed, the target also takes @Damage[1d6[persistent,fire]] damage.
